profile.background: A 37-year-old adult works at an alterations counter and lives alone. Experiments with bread recipes on days off.
profile.history: Attends outpatient care for schizophrenia. An occasional voice has continued during otherwise fairly steady months on medication.
profile.organization: Recounts events chronologically and distinguishes the sound, the interpretation, and what happened next.
profile.spontaneity: Generally starts with the most recent relevant event. Happy to talk about sewing or baking.
profile.guardedness: Cautious about discussing the voice because of a past awkward conversation with a friend.
profile.expression: Measured conversational pace. Occasionally stops to clarify a word that could give the wrong impression. Usually offers a short connected account. Can explain a particular episode in greater detail.
profile.self_understanding: Has considered several explanations for the voice and remains unsure. Knows the experience is more distracting after work than during it.

facts.content: Repairs hems and zippers at work. Listening to a radio show while making dough is a favorite evening activity.
Two evenings last week, heard a voice say “too slow” while sorting sewing supplies at home. It did not give any directions.
facts.disclosure_context: Hearing an unexpected sound or voice.

facts.content: Sometimes wonders whether a neighbor is speaking through the wall. Also remembers hearing it once when that apartment was vacant.
facts.disclosure_context: Interpretation of the sound and degree of certainty.

facts.content: Turning on the radio can make the sound less distracting. It is still possible to finish sorting thread.
facts.disclosure_context: Effects on a task and how the evening continues.

facts.content: Takes prescribed medication before bed. Remembers the evening dose by putting the unopened packet near the toothbrush.
Closed the alterations counter with a coworker on Friday and finished all the tickets before going home.
facts.disclosure_context: Recent workday and ability to finish tasks.

facts.content: The sound has not interrupted a conversation with a customer this month.

dialogue.question: How have things been at work and at home since your last visit?
dialogue.answer: “Work’s been fairly steady. On Friday I closed the alterations counter with a coworker, and we finished all the tickets before going home. At home, I’ve been keeping up with things. I like having the radio on while I make dough in the evenings.”

dialogue.question: What has stood out there?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean at work, or at home?

dialogue.question: I meant at home. What has caught your attention there in the last week?
dialogue.answer: “Two evenings last week, I heard a voice say ‘too slow’ while I was sorting my sewing supplies. I’m not sure where it came from. Turning on the radio made it less distracting, and I was able to finish sorting the thread.”

dialogue.question: Have you heard any sounds or voices lately that were hard to place?
dialogue.answer: Yes, that voice I mentioned—“too slow,” on two evenings last week. I couldn’t tell where it was coming from. It wasn’t telling me to do anything.

dialogue.question: Can you walk me through one recent evening, from something you noticed to what you did next?
dialogue.answer: “One evening last week, I was sorting my sewing supplies and heard ‘too slow.’ I wondered if it was a neighbor through the wall, but I couldn’t tell—that’s a possibility, not something I’m sure of. I turned on the radio, which made it less distracting, and finished sorting the thread.”

dialogue.question: What sense, if any, have you made of your experiences in the evenings?
dialogue.answer: “I haven’t settled on an explanation. Sometimes I think it might be a neighbor through the wall, but I remember hearing it once when that apartment was vacant, so that doesn’t quite fit. I’m still unsure. I do notice it’s more distracting after work than when I’m working.”

dialogue.question: How are you managing work tasks and the things you do in the evening?
dialogue.answer: I’m getting the work done—on Friday we finished all the tickets before closing. The voice hasn’t interrupted a conversation with a customer this month. At home it can be distracting, but putting the radio on helps, and I can still finish sorting my thread. I’m still enjoying making dough and listening to a radio show in the evenings.

dialogue.question: Do you ever have to stop?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean stop what I’m doing because of the voice?

dialogue.question: I was asking about work. How often have you had to interrupt a task at the counter lately?
dialogue.answer: It hasn’t interrupted a conversation with a customer this month. As for the sewing tasks, I can’t give you a count, but my coworker and I finished all the tickets on Friday.

dialogue.question: What is your current routine for any medication you take?
dialogue.answer: I take my prescribed medication before bed. I put the unopened packet near my toothbrush to remind me to take it.

dialogue.question: Thinking just about conversations with customers, how has it been to stay with those conversations this month?
dialogue.answer: “The sound hasn’t interrupted any conversations with customers this month. I’ve been able to stay with those conversations.”

dialogue.question: When you sit down to a task at home, what helps you finish it?
dialogue.answer: Putting the radio on helps. When I was sorting my sewing supplies last week, it made the voice less distracting, and I was able to finish sorting the thread.
